task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of April 14, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The FDA certified NovaBio Therapeutics' manufacturing facility in Westbrook, South Carolina, as Good Manufacturing Practice compliant on April 14, 2025, clearing it to produce mRNA drug substances for commercial use.
The Westbrook facility is the first domestically owned mRNA manufacturing site certified at commercial scale in the United States.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, all mRNA vaccine doses distributed in the U.S. were manufactured at foreign-owned plants or under foreign licensing arrangements.

NovaBio president Dr. Claudia Ferreira said: "This certification means that the next mRNA vaccine or therapy approved in the U.S. can be made here, at scale, without depending on foreign manufacturing partners."
The Westbrook plant has a production capacity of 600 million mRNA doses annually at its current build-out phase.
NovaBio will initially produce drug substance under contract for three pharmaceutical companies that hold their own FDA product approvals; the site is not a drug developer.
GMP certification means the facility's quality systems, environmental controls, and manufacturing records meet federal standards for producing drugs that may be sold in the U.S. market.
mRNA drug manufacturing requires specialized lipid nanoparticle encapsulation equipment and cold-chain-capable fill-finish lines that differ substantially from conventional pharmaceutical production.

James Obi, assistant secretary for manufacturing resilience at the Department of Health and Human Services, said the certification addressed a strategic gap identified in the government's 2023 biomanufacturing security review.
The Westbrook facility received $480 million in federal grants and loan guarantees through the Biomanufacturing Resilience Initiative.
mRNA molecules are highly sensitive to temperature and enzymatic degradation; the Westbrook facility includes dedicated cold-chain storage at minus 80 degrees Celsius.
The certification covered four manufacturing suites; two additional suites are under construction and are expected to be certified by 2027.
The first commercial production run is scheduled to begin in June 2025 for an mRNA-based influenza vaccine candidate that has not yet received market approval.
Dr. Ferreira said the plant's workforce of 340 full-time employees was trained in part through a partnership with two community colleges that developed mRNA technician programs.
Two other mRNA facilities in the U.S. are under construction; neither has received GMP certification.
Federal biodefense planners said the Westbrook plant's surge capacity — its ability to scale up rapidly in a pandemic — is the primary strategic rationale for government investment.
mRNA platform technology, developed originally for cancer immunotherapy, was adapted for infectious disease vaccines and received Emergency Use Authorization during the COVID-19 pandemic.
NovaBio's contract clients include two U.S.-based pharmaceutical firms and one European company with FDA-approved mRNA products.
The FDA inspection that preceded certification lasted nine days and covered raw material traceability, batch record systems, and clean room environmental monitoring.

Obi said the government plans to exercise a reserve capacity clause in its agreement with NovaBio, which requires the facility to be available for government mRNA production within 60 days of a declared public health emergency.

a statement that NovaBio develops its own mRNA drugs
a COVID vaccine dose count not in the notes
